messages.subject: user defined functions library
parts:
I think we should host a repository of useful user-defined functions, perhaps separated into distributions, rngs, and operations. Even if it takes a while to build up a sizable library this would eventually be a very helpful resource for users. If I set this up should it go under the BSD or CC-BY license?

Jonah

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] user defined functions library
parts:
Hi Jonah,

Thanks for bringing this up. I've been thinking having a "cookbook" would be useful. Some thoughts:
- I'd suggest a separate repo. Something that's strictly controlled with consistent formatting, a high level of certainty before it gets in.
- Stan: I think we should revisit how to include files.
- Math: I think we should expose all our check functions.
- Stan: I think we should have a unit testing framework for Stan functions. This last one will be to demonstrate that the functions being submitted are actually sound and can be trusted.


Unit testing for Stan functions. I'm not certain about all the details, but perhaps we can have:

// foo.stan
functions {
   real bar(real baz, vector qux) {
       ...
       return value;
   }
}

// foo.test.stan?
#include foo.stan
transformed data {
  real baz1;
  real baz2;
  vector qux1;
  vector qux2;
  baz1 = 1;
  baz2 = 2;
  ...
}
transformed parameters {
  real baz3;
  vector qux3;
  ...
}
test {
   EXPECT_EQ(123, bar(baz1, qux1));
   EXPECT_EQ(456, bar(baz2, qux2));
}
test {
   EXPECT_REJECT(bar(infinity(), qux1));
}
test {
   real norf;
   norf = bar(baz3, qux3);
   EXPECT_EQ(789, norf);

   EXPECT_EQ(0, gradient(norf, baz3));
   EXPECT_EQ({1, 2, 3}, gradient(norf, qux3));
}
//


I'm not really fond of the all caps, so please look at the function and not the form. I think using a unit testing framework that outlines what we expect is going to be the right way to go.

I can see the tests being generated as C++ that could either be run from the command line after built or run within the interfaces. If those are strict requirements, we can design for that.



Daniel

Stan programs, right? (Though I agree that includes for
Stan C++ would be good and exposing all the validation functions
would go a long way to allowing users to write robust argument
checking.)

case studies --- take them from contributors and see how it
goes. So they could go in example-models or a new repo.
This all needs to get a bit more organized, but I think that's
hard to anticipate until it gets a bit bigger.

If we have to wait for a unit testing framework in Stan, that'll
probably be a while.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] user defined functions library
parts: On Sun, Mar 13, 2016 at 9:49 PM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
I'd prefer a new repo. Or calling example-models something else.
I agree that it should be separate from example-models. Maybe stan-function-library?

I don't think we should wait, but I think the functions should be tested. I'm assuming we are thinking this is a validated set of functions that were collecting. If I've misunderstood the scope, please let me know.

Yeah, that's what I have in mind. I'm not sure how much effort it would take to do C++ testing, and I would understand if people want to avoid R, but it would be pretty easy to do testing using RStan's expose_stan_functions. There could be an R script that brings the function(s) into R using expose_stan_functions and then runs some tests in R.
